scenes.tts: A creek is full of tiny animals hiding under the rocks. They eat bits of leaves, and fish eat them, so they all need each other. Some only live in clean water, so they are clues to how healthy the creek is.

scenes.tts: You need a kitchen strainer or small net, a white tray, a plastic spoon, and closed toe water shoes for everyone.
scenes.narration: You need a kitchen strainer or small net, a white tray, a plastic spoon, and closed toe water shoes for everyone.

scenes.tts: Pick a creek with a shallow riffle, low and clear, at least three days after heavy rain. Fill the tray with creek water, about two to three centimeters deep.

items.text: A shallow riffle, low clear creek
3 or more days after heavy rain

scenes.narration: Pick a creek with a shallow riffle, low and clear, at least three days after heavy rain. Fill the tray with creek water, about two to three centimeters deep.

scenes.tts: Hold the strainer just downstream of a rock while someone lifts the rock and rubs its underside. Tip the strainer into the tray. After a minute, specks will start to move. Finding many different kinds is usually a sign of a healthy creek.
scenes.narration: Hold the strainer just downstream of a rock while someone lifts the rock and rubs its underside. Tip the strainer into the tray. After a minute, specks will start to move. Finding many different kinds is usually a sign of a healthy creek.

scenes.tts: Stay within arm's reach of your child the whole time they are in or beside the water. Wade only where the water is ankle deep, and slow, never rushing.

items.text: Arm's reach; ankle-deep, slow water only

scenes.line: Creek animals need each other, and some are clues to clean water.
